solution: Find vertices: \(L_1\cap L_2\): \(2x=0 \Rightarrow x=0, y=4\). \(L_1\cap L_3\): \(2y=0 \Rightarrow y=0, x=4\). \(L_2\cap L_3\): \(3x+y=4, x+3y=4 \Rightarrow x=y=1\). Distances: \(d_{12}=\sqrt{16+16}=4\sqrt2\); \(d_{13}=\sqrt{1+9}=\sqrt{10}\); \(d_{23}=\sqrt{9+1}=\sqrt{10}\). Two sides are equal, so the triangle is isosceles. Matches option A.
note: side lengths: d13 = d23 = sqrt10 (was 4sqrt2 and 3sqrt2)

solution: The triangle is right angled at \(O(0,0)\). Therefore the orthocentre is \(O(0,0)\) and the circumcentre is the mid-point of the hypotenuse, i.e. \(\left(\frac{b}{2}, \frac{a}{2}\right)\). Therefore the distance between the orthocentre and the circumcentre \(= \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\).
note: circumcentre is (b/2, a/2), midpoint of (0,a) and (b,0)

solution:
Take \(A(0,0)\), \(B(3,4)\) and \(C(4,0)\). \(AC\) lies on the \(x\)-axis, so the altitude \(BD\) from \(B\) is the vertical line \(x = 3\) ...(i).

Slope of \(BC = \frac{0 - 4}{4 - 3} = -4\), so the altitude \(AE \perp BC\) through \(A\) has slope \(\frac{1}{4}\): \(x - 4y = 0\) ...(ii).

From (i) and (ii), \(x = 3,\ y = \frac{3}{4}\).

\(\therefore\) the orthocentre of the triangle is \(\left(3, \frac{3}{4}\right)\).
note: altitude BD is x = 3 (AC is the x-axis), not 3x + 4y = 12

solution:
Co-ordinates of the vertices of the square are \(A(0,0),\ B(0,1),\ C(1,1)\) and \(D(1,0).\)

Now the equation of AC is \(y = x\) and of BD is \(y - 1 = \  - \frac{1}{1}\ (x - 0) \Rightarrow x + y = 1\)

solution:
Let the point be (x,y) which is equidistant from (a+b, a-b) and (b-a, a+b).

Then, \(\sqrt{\{\left( x - (a + b) \right\}^{2} + \left\{ y - (a - b) \right\}^{2}}\)

\(= \sqrt{\{\left( x - (b - a) \right\}^{2} + \left\{ y - (a + b) \right\}^{2}}\)

On squaring,

\(x^{2} + (a + b)^{2} - 2x\ (a + b) + y^{2} + (a - b)^{2} - 2y\ (a - b)\) \(= x^{2} + (b - a)^{2} - 2x(b - a) + y^{2} + (a + b)^{2} - 2(a + b)y\)

\(\Rightarrow 2x\ (b - a - a - b) = 2y\ (a - b - a - b)\)

\(\Rightarrow 4ax = 4by\)

\(\Rightarrow ax - by = 0\ or - ax + by = 0\)
note: typo b(b - a) -> (b - a)

solution:
The points are collinear when the slope from \((-5, 1)\) to \((p, 5)\) equals the slope from \((-5, 1)\) to \((10, 7)\).

Slope \(= \frac{7 - 1}{10 + 5} = \frac{6}{15} = \frac{2}{5}\), so \(\frac{5 - 1}{p + 5} = \frac{2}{5}\), that is \(p + 5 = 10\) and \(p = 5\).

solution: Slope of first diagonal: \(\frac{1}{2}\). Slope of second: \(-2\). Product \(=-1\), so diagonals are perpendicular. A rhombus has perpendicular diagonals, so \(ABCD\) may be a rhombus (it is one when the diagonals also bisect each other). A rectangle's diagonals are perpendicular only when it is a square, and a general parallelogram's never are.
note: perpendicular diagonals do not make a rhombus on their own; the question asks 'may be'

solution:
Area of triangle \(= \frac{1}{2}\left|x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)\right|\).

Here \(y_2 - y_3 = 4\lambda - 6\), \(y_3 - y_1 = 4\) and \(y_1 - y_2 = 2 - 4\lambda\), so twice the area is \(\left|\lambda(4\lambda - 6) + 4(1 - \lambda) - (4 + \lambda)(2 - 4\lambda)\right| = \left|8\lambda^{2} + 4\lambda - 4\right|\).

Area 70 gives \(8\lambda^{2} + 4\lambda - 4 = \pm 140\). With \(+140\): \(2\lambda^{2} + \lambda - 36 = 0\), so \(\lambda = 4\) or \(\lambda = -\frac{9}{2}\). With \(-140\): \(2\lambda^{2} + \lambda + 34 = 0\), which has no real root.

So there is exactly one integral value, \(\lambda = 4\).
note: rewritten: expansion was wrong (roots are 4 and -9/2, not 4.186 and -4.061)

solution: Line equation: \(x\cos15^{\circ}+y\sin15^{\circ}=4\). Intercepts: \(x\)-intercept \(=4/\cos15^{\circ}\), \(y\)-intercept \(=4/\sin15^{\circ}\). Sum \(=4\left(\frac{1}{\cos15^{\circ}}+\frac{1}{\sin15^{\circ}}\right)=4\cdot\frac{\sin15^{\circ}+\cos15^{\circ}}{\sin15^{\circ}\cos15^{\circ}}=4\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}\sin60^{\circ}}{\sin30^{\circ}/2}=4\cdot\frac{\sqrt{6}/2}{1/4}=8\sqrt{6}\). Common mistake: using complementary angles incorrectly.

solution: The line passes through \((1, 0)\) and \((-2, \sqrt{3})\). Slope \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{\sqrt{3} - 0}{-2 - 1} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\). The angle \(\theta\) the line makes with the \(x\)-axis (\(0^{\circ} \le \theta < 180^{\circ}\)) has \(\tan\theta = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), so \(\theta = 180^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 150^{\circ}\).
note: arctan(-1/sqrt3) is -30 degrees; the inclination is 150 degrees

solution:
Let \(A(x,y)\) be the required point.

\(\therefore\ PA = 2 \cdot AQ\)

Thus, \(A\) divides \(PQ\) internally or externally in the ratio \(2:1\).

If \(A\) divides \(PQ\) internally in the ratio \(2:1\), then coordinates of \(A\) are

\(\begin{matrix} & x = \frac{2 \times ( - 2) + 1 \times 3}{2 + 1}\text{~and~}y = \frac{2 \times 5 + 1 \times ( - 4)}{2 + 1} \\ \Rightarrow & x = - \frac{1}{3}\text{~and~}y = 2 \end{matrix}\)

\(\therefore\) Coordinates of \(A\) are \(\left( - \frac{1}{3},2 \right)\).

Again, if \(A\) divides \(PQ\) externally in the ratio \(2:1\), then coordinates of \(A\) are

\(\begin{matrix} & \ x = \frac{2 \times ( - 2) - 1 \times 3}{2 - 1}\text{~and~}y = \frac{2 \times 5 - 1 \times ( - 4)}{2 - 1} \\ & \  \Rightarrow \ x = - 7\text{~and~}y = 14 \\ & \ \therefore\text{~Coordinates of~}A\text{~are~}( - 7,14). \end{matrix}\)
note: PA = 2AQ (was PA = 2PQ); stray 'Solution (a)**' removed

solution:
\(AB = \sqrt{(4 + 1)^{2} + (0 + 1)^{2}} = \sqrt{26};\)

\(BC = \sqrt{(3 + 1)^{2} + (5 + 1)^{2}} = \sqrt{52}\)

\(CA = \sqrt{(4 - 3)^{2} + (0 - 5)^{2}} = \sqrt{26}\ ;\)

In isosceles triangle side \(AB = CA\)

For right angled triangle, \(BC^{2} = AB^{2} + AC^{2}\)

So, here \(BC = \sqrt{52}\ or\ BC^{2} = 52\)

or \(\left( \sqrt{26} \right)^{2} + \left( \sqrt{26} \right)^{2} = 52\)

So, the given triangle is right angled and also isosceles
note: CA is sqrt26, so 26 + 26 = 52

solution: Let the coordinates of the point \(P\) which divides the line joining \((1,0)\) and \((2cos\theta,2sin\theta)\) in the ratio \(2:3\) be \((h,k)\). Then, \(h = \frac{4cos\theta + 3}{5}\) and \(k = \frac{4sin\theta}{5}\) \(\Rightarrow cos\theta = \frac{5h - 3}{4}\) and \(sin\theta = \frac{5k}{4}\) \(\Rightarrow \left( \frac{5h - 3}{4} \right)^{2} + \left( \frac{5k}{4} \right)^{2} = 1 \Rightarrow (5h - 3)^{2} + (5k)^{2} = 16\) Therefore locus of \((h,k)\) is \((5x - 3)^{2} + (5y)^{2} = 16\), which is a circle.

If \(3, x_1, x_2\) and \(4, y_1, y_2\) are each in A.P. with common differences \(d\) and \(e\), then \(B = (3 + d, 4 + e)\) and \(C = (3 + 2d, 4 + 2e)\). So \(\overrightarrow{AC} = 2\,\overrightarrow{AB}\), and \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) lie on one line. Hence (B), collinear.
note: B is one step from A and C two steps, not equal increments

solution:
Equation of a circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x + 2y = 0\)

\(x(x - 6) + y(y + 2) = 0\)

This is the equation of a circle in diameter form, where end points of diameter are (0,0) and (6,-2).

So, equation of diameter, \(y - 0 = \frac{- 2}{6}\ (x - 0) \Rightarrow x + 3y = 0\)
note: the diameter passes through the origin: (x - 0), not (x - 2)

solution:
\(x^{2} + y^{2} = 4\) ...(i)

\(x + y = 2\) ...(ii)

\(\because x^{2} + y^{2} = (x + y)^{2} - 2xy\)

\(\Rightarrow 4 = 4 - 2xy\)

\(\Rightarrow xy = 0\) ...(iii)

Values satisfying Eqs. (i), (ii) and (iii) are (2,0) and (0,2): with \(xy = 0\) one coordinate is 0, and then \(x + y = 2\) makes the other 2
note: only (2,0) and (0,2) satisfy x + y = 2

solution:
Area of \(\triangle ABD = \frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{matrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{4}{3} & 1 \\ -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{7}{3} & 1 \end{matrix}\right| = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{35}{9} - \frac{8}{9}\right) = \frac{3}{2}\) sq units.

So the area of parallelogram \(ABCD = 2 \times \frac{3}{2} = 3\) sq units.
